reviewEvidence.visualReviewMethod: Full-duration six-second contacts; English burned-in points and Pyra before/after poses inspected; not continuous audio/all-frame review.
reviewEvidence.resolutionNote: Research-only reference media; never a production source. Independent production footage still requires genuine FHD or higher.

centralQuestion: What makes the pose at the instant of contact read as a clear, convincing attack?
thesis: Build the contact pose for the actual gameplay view: readable amplitude, aligned attack direction, deliberate asymmetry/twist, a convincing contact moment, and a clear silhouette under the camera's perspective.

claims: Attack animation strongly affects a combat game's feel.
This lesson isolates the contact pose rather than the entire action.
Hit stop makes the contact composition especially memorable, so pose references should capture that moment.
sections.observedVisuals: Captain Falcon/Ness and Ridley/Diddy contact images precede a figure-reference explanation.
sections.ownScreenProposal: Independent real contact example, then freeze our grid character at its own contact frame and label the exact pose under review.
prerequisites: Hit stop as a brief visual hold
sections.transitionToNext: Because this short pose receives disproportionate attention, it needs several concrete readability checks.

claims: Use enough exaggeration for the movement to remain legible at a distance.
sections.observedVisuals: Wide gameplay camera with small characters.
sections.ownScreenProposal: Same grid pose at inspection size and actual gameplay-sized inset; amplify only its main line of action.
sections.transitionToNext: Large motion still needs to travel through the intended contact region.

claims: Keep an attack aligned with its intended fighting plane; a move directed too far toward or away from the camera can fail to match the contact it should communicate.
sections.observedVisuals: Overhead Link attack with a central guide demonstrates the depth relationship.
sections.ownScreenProposal: Keep main side view and add an observer top view with a shared grid. Show sword path leaving and then crossing the relevant interaction plane. The plane/hit region belongs to our demonstration, not invented commercial telemetry.
prerequisites: Define screen depth and fighting plane visibly before using axis letters.
sections.transitionToNext: Once the direction is clear, the body's arrangement needs enough visual character.

claims: Avoid mechanically symmetrical poses unless the symmetry is an intentional comic or stylistic choice.
A torso shown perfectly side-on often benefits from a small twist for greater clarity and contrast.
sections.observedVisuals: Donkey Kong's asymmetric shoulders/arms are marked; Wario demonstrates deliberate symmetry; Shulk torso example follows.
sections.ownScreenProposal: One mannequin and camera: symmetric pose→offset limbs→small torso twist, changing only one element per reveal.
sections.transitionToNext: The readable pose must also occur at the right point in the swing.

claims: For a sword swing, where possible place hit stop after some visible follow-through of the swing.
Stopping before the sword has convincingly moved through contact can weaken the impression of a hit.
sections.observedVisuals: Pyra/Mario adjacent contact moments compare how far the sword has swung.
sections.ownScreenProposal: Scrub our same sword path to two nearby candidate contact poses, then replay both at normal speed; mark them as design alternatives.
sections.transitionToNext: A convincing pose in the center of the screen must survive the camera's other viewpoints too.

claims: Check some variation in perspective; left and right sides of the game camera can change how a pose appears.
sections.observedVisuals: Two Kirby positions at opposite ends of a stage.
sections.ownScreenProposal: Show our posed character at left/center/right under the same perspective camera; do not rotate the camera arbitrarily and call it the same test.
prerequisites: Perspective means the apparent angle depends on the viewing position; demonstrate before naming it.
sections.transitionToNext: Across those views, the main test is whether the silhouette remains understandable.

claims: Keep limbs and overall silhouette clearly readable.
A side-view game especially depends on its side-view silhouette.
Small changes to a pose can materially improve the outline.
sections.observedVisuals: Link separated against dark background, Palutena side-view action, then Pyra pre-feedback/post-feedback comparison with a small twist and leg/torso relationship change.
sections.ownScreenProposal: Render our same contact pose as a flat silhouette on the grid; change the overlapping limb/torso arrangement, show outlines before/after, then restore materials and replay.
sections.exampleRoles: Pyra is a concrete revision showing the checklist changes a real pose rather than remaining abstract advice.
sections.transitionToNext: Recognizing these differences improves through posing and checking actual forms.

claims: Manipulating a physical articulated form helps develop judgment for strong poses.
sections.observedVisuals: Presenter closes by encouraging hands-on pose practice.
sections.ownScreenProposal: Our own articulated model passes through two purposeful alternative poses, then settles on the final checked attack pose.
sections.transitionToNext: Close on the improved contact pose and the observable reason it reads better.

omissionsAndReasons: Remove presenter attribution and personal supervision framing; preserve the actual before/after lesson using independently authored poses.
Keep the intentional-symmetry condition because it defines the guidance's scope, not as a generic defensive caveat.
